newsitem.title: EGYPT: Agip well has oil in Gulf of Suez.
newsitem.headline: Agip well has oil in Gulf of Suez.

text.p: Petrobel/Belayim Petroleum, a joint venture between the Egyptian state and Agip SpA of Italy, has found oil in a newly drilled well in the Belayim concession in the Gulf of Suez, the Oil Ministry said on Monday.

The oil is at a depth of 3,480 metres (11,400 feet) in a layer 70 metres (230 feet) thick, it said. The indications are that the well, known as 79/113, can produce 1,000 barrels of crude a day, it added.
An Agip official said the well was close to the existing Belayim field, which has been producing for many years. He declined to say how significant he thought it might be.
Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi has given instructions that the well go into production immediately because it is close to existing production facilities, the ministry said.
